name: Andromeda Galaxy
tagline: The farthest thing you can see unaided — two and a half million years of light away.
history: Persian astronomer Al-Sufi recorded Andromeda as a 'little cloud' around 964 CE — making it one of the earliest documented deep-sky objects and still the most distant thing visible to the naked eye. For centuries it was called a spiral nebula inside our own galaxy, until Edwin Hubble identified Cepheid variable stars in it in 1924 and measured its distance — proof that the universe extends far beyond the Milky Way, a discovery that rewrote cosmology overnight. It holds about a trillion stars, roughly double our galaxy, and blueshifted spectra show it approaching at 110 km/s: the two spirals will begin merging in about 4.5 billion years.
